title: Alljoined-1.6M
description: Alljoined-1.6M is a large-scale EEG dataset capturing neural responses to rapid serial visual presentation (RSVP) of natural images from the THINGS database, recorded from 20 healthy adults using a consumer-grade 32-channel EMOTIV FLEX2 system. Each participant completed four sessions, yielding over 1.6 million stimulus trials in total, with an embedded oddball detection task to maintain engagement. The dataset was designed to evaluate whether affordable, consumer-grade EEG hardware can support deep learning-based brain-computer interface and semantic decoding research comparable to costlier research-grade systems.
methods_description: EEG was recorded using the EMOTIV FLEX2 wireless 32-channel system (sintered Ag/AgCl gel electrodes) at 256 Hz, following the extended 10-20 montage focused on occipital/visual regions. Participants viewed images from the THINGS database presented for 100 ms each in an RSVP paradigm (200 ms cycle), performing an orthogonal oddball detection task (detecting a Woody character in ~6% of trials) across four sessions per participant, each comprising 19 runs (~5 minutes each). Raw data were exported as EDF files with only the 32 EEG channels retained, and converted to BIDS format using MNE-BIDS.
